history.summary: Revered Kali shrine on Kalibari Road (NH 208A) in Dharmanagar, North Tripura, featured on the North Tripura district government website as a 'spiritual haven'. 'Kalibari' means the abode of Goddess Kali; the temple has simple architecture, well-maintained premises, and becomes a festival hub during Kali Puja and Durga Puja. IDENTITY CAVEAT: several Kalibaris exist in and around Dharmanagar (e.g. Nayapara Kalibari near the market, and a Kalibari at Kadamtala ~9 km away) — this file documents the prominent Kalibari Temple on Kalibari Road per the district website and travel guides. Opening hours conflict: 5 AM–9 PM per travel guides vs 5 PM–10 PM on one map listing — verify locally.

name: Kalibari Temple, Dharmanagar
town_description: Dharmanagar is the headquarters of North Tripura district, a municipal town near the Assam border in the northernmost part of the state; it is Tripura's second town by road/rail connectivity after Agartala and a gateway to the Jampui Hills and Unakoti.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~180–200 km) or Silchar Airport, Assam (~120 km)
travel.railway: Dharmanagar railway station; trains connect Silchar and Agartala
travel.road: Silchar–Dharmanagar ~120 km (~3 hours); Agartala–Dharmanagar ~200 km (~8–9 hours)

visitor_information.best_time: October–March (pleasant winter weather); Diwali/Kali Puja and Navaratri are the most festive periods
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5 AM–9 PM per travel guides (one map listing says 5 PM–10 PM — verify locally)
